studies.Population: Male smokers aged 50–69 years enrolled in the ATBC Study; aggressive cases were defined by TNM stage III–IV, AJCC stage >=3, or Gleason sum >=8
studies.Reference: Metabolomic analysis of prostate cancer risk in a prospective cohort: The alpha-tocopherol, beta-carotene cancer prevention (ATBC) study.
studies.Authors: Mondul AM, Moore SC, Weinstein SJ, Karoly ED, Sampson JN, Albanes D
studies.Design: Prospective nested case-control study within the ATBC cohort
studies.Timing: Prediagnostic fasting serum collected up to 20 years before prostate-cancer diagnosis
studies.comparison_type: Per 1-standard-deviation increase in serum metabolite level versus a 1-standard-deviation lower level; aggressive prostate cancer cases versus matched controls
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Ultrahigh performance liquid chromatography/mass spectroscopy and gas chromatography/mass spectroscopy identified 626 compounds

sample_size.excerpt: To this end, we conducted a prospective analysis of prostate cancer within the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study cohort based on 200 cases (100 aggressive) and 200 controls (age- and blood collection date-matched) with fasting serum collected up to 20 years prior to case diagnoses. Ultrahigh performance liquid chromatography/mass spectroscopy and gas chromatography/mass spectroscopy identified 626 compounds detected in >95% of the men and the odds ratio per 1-standard deviation increase in log-metabolite levels and risk were estimated using conditional logistic regression.
sample_size.location: Methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 200 + 200 = 400

cases.excerpt: To this end, we conducted a prospective analysis of prostate cancer within the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study cohort based on 200 cases (100 aggressive) and 200 controls (age- and blood collection date-matched) with fasting serum collected up to 20 years prior to case diagnoses.

effect_size.excerpt: Inositol-1-phosphate showed the strongest association (OR = 0.56, 95% CI = 0.39-0.81, p = 0.002) and glycerophospholipids and fatty acids were heavily represented; e.g., oleoyl-linoleoyl-glycerophosphoinositol (OR = 0.64, p = 0.004), 1-stearoylglycerophosphoglycerol (OR=0.65, p = 0.025), stearate (OR=0.65, p = 0.010) and docosadienoate (OR = 0.66, p = 0.014).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Inositol-1-phosphate showed the strongest association (OR = 0.56, 95% CI = 0.39-0.81, p = 0.002) and glycerophospholipids and fatty acids were heavily represented; e.g., oleoyl-linoleoyl-glycerophosphoinositol (OR = 0.64, p = 0.004), 1-stearoylglycerophosphoglycerol (OR=0.65, p = 0.025), stearate (OR=0.65, p = 0.010) and docosadienoate (OR = 0.66, p = 0.014).

disease_scope_review.endpoint_excerpt: We observed strong inverse associations between energy and lipid metabolites and aggressive cancer (p = 0.018 and p = 0.041, respectively, for chemical class over-representation). Inositol-1-phosphate showed the strongest association (OR = 0.56, 95% CI = 0.39-0.81, p = 0.002) and glycerophospholipids and fatty acids were heavily represented; e.g., oleoyl-linoleoyl-glycerophosphoinositol (OR = 0.64, p = 0.004), 1-stearoylglycerophosphoglycerol (OR=0.65, p = 0.025), stearate (OR=0.65, p = 0.010) and docosadienoate (OR = 0.66, p = 0.014).
disease_scope_review.reason: The inositol-1-phosphate estimate is presented within the abstract's aggressive-cancer results and is based on prediagnostic serum, supporting an aggressive incident endpoint.
